To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the MXAN procedure allows one to extract structural information from the XANES of metalloprotenins and that, for the case of Mb*CO, this method provides a quantitative description of the Fe-CO local structure.

the MXAN method can provide accurate quantitative structural information from XANES spectra, that the Fe K-edge of Mb*CO has been successfully analysed using this method and that the extracted local structure is in excellent agreement with the one obtained from EXAFS and X-ray diffraction data.
we have developed a new method for quantitative analysis of polarized XANES data, and that this new method has allowed us to extract the local structure of the Fe-CO bond in MbCO and Mb*CO.

the development and application of new techniques in the field of the X-ray absorption spectroscopy of biological systems.
the development of new methods for the analysis of X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) data.
the development and application of a new method to extract structural information from XANES spectra.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

MXAN is a very useful method for the quantitative analysis of XANES data, and that it is able to provide a reliable and quantitative determination of the local geometry of metalloprotesins, even in the case of complex systems.

the MXAN method is a powerful new tool for the quantitative analysis of XANES spectra and the determination of the local structure of metalloprotein sites, with an accuracy that is limited only by the quality of the experimental data.

, although the XANES technique does not allow a direct determination of the Fe-CO distance and the Fe-C-O bending angle, it is able to provide information about the Fe-C-O angle and to determine the orientation of the Fe-C vector with respect to the heme plane.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have been able to determine the structure of a metalloproteine in the ground state and the photoproduct.
the MXAN method allows us to extract structural information from the XANES spectrum of the Fe site in Mb*CO and MbCO with a precision that is comparable to that obtained from the EXAFS analysis.
we developed a new fitting procedure, named the MXAN, for quantitative analysis of XANES spectra, and applied it to the Fe K-edge XANES of MbCO and Mb*CO.
The main takeaway from our work is that

XANES spectroscopy can provide structural information that is complementary to EXAFS, and that it is possible to obtain quantitative information on the geometry of a metal site in a metalloprotein by using the full multiple-scatter approach in combination with a new fitting procedure.
the MXAN method is able to extract structural information from XANES spectra with an accuracy of the order of the experimental error, which is of the order of 0.1 A for the distances.
MXAN is a powerful method for the quantitative analysis of the XANES region of the X-ray absorption spectrum.
